introduction: On this Sunday, Ezekiel tells us that if a wicked person turns from sin, they will live. In the Gospel, Jesus tells of two sons: one says no to his father but then goes to work in the vineyard; the other says yes but does not go. Paul urges us to have the same mind as Christ, who humbled himself. Let us turn to God not only in words but in deeds.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord is good and upright; he shows sinners the way. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may live with the humility and unity of Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who have said no to God: that, like the first son, they may change their minds and return. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those whose faith is only in words: that it may become real in their actions. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who look down on sinners: that they may discover that God welcomes all who repent. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may count others better than ourselves and look to their interests. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you welcome every sinner who turns back to you. Give us the mind of Christ, so that our yes to you may be true in our deeds. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Two sons
reflection.body:
Some of the people in Ezekiel's time complain that God is unfair. God answers that the way is open for everyone: "when the wicked man turns away from his wickedness that he has committed, and does that which is lawful and right, he will save his soul alive." No one is defined forever by their past. Conversion is always possible.

In the Gospel, Jesus tells a short parable to the religious leaders. A father asks his first son to go and work in the vineyard. The son says, "I will not," but later changes his mind and goes. The father asks his second son, who answers politely, "I'm going, sir," but never goes. Jesus asks, "Which of the two did the will of his father?" They answer, "The first."

Then Jesus makes his point: "the tax collectors and the prostitutes are entering into God's Kingdom before you." They had said no to God by their lives, but when John the Baptist preached, they repented. The religious leaders had said yes in words but did not change.

The parable invites us to look honestly at ourselves. Many of us are like the second son: we say the right words, go to church, pray our prayers, but some part of our lives has not yet said yes to God. Others may be like the first son: their lives once said no, but they are turning back. What matters is not our words but our actions.

Paul shows us the mind of Christ: "doing nothing through rivalry or through conceit, but in humility, each counting others better than himself." And he gives us the great hymn of Christ who "emptied himself, taking the form of a servant."

This week, find one area of your life where you have said yes to God in words but not in deeds, and take a concrete step to change. And pray for someone who has said no to God: they may yet change their mind.
